y1: At that time, wealth consisted of expensive clothes, grain, and money. A moth would eat the clothes, insects would eat the grain, and thieves would break through mud walls and enter the house.
y2: “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” If we look at what we spend our time and money on, we will see where our heart is.
y3: Treasure in heaven is not just a reward received after death. Helping the poor (19:21), loving God, and leading people to salvation already carry eternal value right now.
y5: “The lamp of the body is the eye.” In Hebrew idioms, a “healthy eye” meant generosity, while a “bad eye” meant stinginess.
y6: “No one can serve two masters. You cannot serve both God and wealth.” Here, “to serve” means that a slave belongs to his master.
y7: “Wealth” is “mammon” in Aramaic. Jesus names money as a person competing with God. Money is a good servant, but a bad master.
y9: “Don't be anxious for your life, what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear.” Jesus tells us to look at the birds in the sky and the lilies in the field.
y10: “Which of you by being anxious can add one moment to his lifespan?” Worry changes nothing; it only takes away the joy of today.
y11: Jesus's logic goes from “lesser to greater.” If God clothes even the grass that is here today and thrown into the oven tomorrow, how much more will He care for His children. The opposite of worry is not irresponsibility, but trust.
y13: The pagans run after all these things, but your heavenly Father knows that you need them. “But seek first God's Kingdom and His righteousness.”
y14: “Therefore don't be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day's own evil is sufficient.”
y15: “Seek first the Kingdom” is connected to “Let Your Kingdom come” in the Lord's Prayer, and “knows your needs” is connected to “Give us our daily bread.” Turning worry into prayer is Jesus's way (Phil. 4:6).
verse: “But seek first God's Kingdom and His righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well. Therefore don't be anxious for tomorrow.”
prayer: My heavenly Father, I believe that You, who feed the birds and dress the wildflowers, care for me even more. Free me from the worries that divide my heart and from the mastery of money. Help me to live today by seeking Your Kingdom and righteousness first. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: moth. In an era when expensive clothes were considered great wealth, moths silently destroyed fortunes. James 5:2 also says, “your garments are moth-eaten.”
d1: wealth. A word referring to money and all property. Jesus calls it a “master” that can be served. The same word is found in Luke 16:13.
d2: be anxious. A state where the heart is torn in different directions. It appears six times in 6:25–34. “Casting all your worries on him” (1 Peter 5:7).
d3: righteousness. The theme of the entire Sermon on the Mount. It is a life lived rightly under God's rule. “Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness” (5:6).
